headline: China accuses US warship of 'illegally' entering Spratly waters
dek: China's Southern Theater Command Navy accused US littoral combat ship USS Charleston of jeopardising maritime security by 'illegally' entering waters near Sabina Shoal in the Spratly Islands without Beijing's approval; PLAN forces tracked and monitored it. US Navy did not immediately respond.
sources: Reuters (Liz Lee, Beijing newsroom) quoting China's Southern Theater Command Navy
fault_line: Routine freedom-of-navigation defence vs deliberate escalation near a disputed reef while the US is stretched in the Gulf

sections.what_happened: China's Southern Theater Command Navy accused US littoral combat ship USS Charleston of jeopardising maritime security by 'illegally' entering waters near Sabina Shoal in the Spratly Islands without Beijing's approval; PLAN forces tracked and monitored it. US Navy did not immediately respond.
sections.what_verified: Reuters text (wtbx.com syndication, reuters.com URL); corroborating detail from Philippines mutual-defence-treaty context; Taiwan/Philippines outlets carry the Chinese statement
sections.what_disputed: US Navy no comment yet; China and the Philippines both claim Sabina Shoal — China calls it 'sovereign waters', a claim not recognised by Manila or Washington
sections.why_matters: Map explainer: while the world watches Hormuz, the US sailed into China's most disputed shoal — who actually claims Sabina, and why Beijing chose to announce it today
sections.context: Background: USS Charleston FONOP near Sabina Shoal: China accuses US warship of 'illegally' entering Spratly waters
